results.title: Playback User Guide
results.summary: The master user guide. Relevant documented points: the Audio Device setting (Settings > General > Audio Device) chooses the device Playback uses for all audio output; Auto Pan sends click/guide left and tracks right on the headphone output; MultiOuts (Premium) allow up to 32 outputs; track routing lives in Settings > Tracks and bus routing in Settings > Buses; purchased tracks download free; downloaded setlists stay on the device until removed or until a different user signs in; Settings > About has Manage Subscription and Restore Purchases.

steps.text: Select the output device: tap the stack icon (top-right) > Settings > General > Audio Device.

Auto Pan: Settings > General > Auto-Pan. Sends click and guide to the left output and all tracks to the right output of the device's stereo output, so you can run tracks from the headphone port without an interface.
Track routing: Settings > Tracks, tap an instrument part and choose a bus. Routing is device-specific and applies to that track across all songs and setlists on that device.
Bus routing: Settings > Buses, tap a bus cell, choose an output, tap Done. Swipe left on a bus to edit its name/abbreviation. Bus routing is saved per audio device.
If an output is greyed out it may be in use by SMPTE: change the SMPTE routing or disable SMPTE output in General settings.

Download a song: when adding a song, tap Add in the top-right corner. In the Setlists menu, tap Open Setlist, select a setlist, and tap the download icons to download tracks without loading the setlist, or load it to download every song automatically. Songs already on the device from another setlist show no download icon.

Remove one setlist from the device: open it in the Setlists menu and choose Remove Setlist From Device. Remove all: Setlists menu > Delete All Setlists From Device. This does not delete setlists from your MultiTracks.com account; re-download from the setlist menu to recover.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: Subscription not recognized: Settings > About > Restore Purchases. The guide says: if an iTunes subscription is expired or not being confirmed by Playback, reconcile any payment issues in the App Store and tap Restore Purchases to reconnect your In-App Subscription.
steps.caution: Updating the app closes Playback and takes a few minutes; don't do this during a service.

steps.text: Side menu (stack icon) shows user name, organization name and ID, Switch Organizations, and Log Out.
steps.caution: Signing out can interrupt cloud access until you sign back in.

results.title: How to Use Playback with Your Sound System
results.summary: Three documented ways to get audio out of Playback: the built-in headphone port with Auto-Pan (2 channels: click/guide left, tracks right), a USB audio interface (up to 32 outputs, grouped into mono or stereo buses), and networked audio such as Dante or SoundGrid (iPad/iPhone limited to two channels; macOS can route up to 32 via Dante Virtual Soundcard). Bluetooth, subscription tiers, and menu paths are not covered here.

requirements.text: Using independent bus routing and MultiOuts is a Playback Premium feature. The hardware output count alone does not establish that this feature is unlocked. This condition applies to the MultiOuts method, not every basic two-feed Auto-Pan goal.

steps.text: Option 1 - headphone port: Auto-Pan is on by default. Use a 1/8" TRS to dual 1/4" TS cable, a stereo DI (or two mono DIs) to convert to XLR, then XLR to the stage box. Devices without a headphone jack can use a Lightning-to-3.5mm or USB-C-to-3.5mm adapter. Left channel feeds in-ears (click/guide); right feeds the house mix.

Option 2 - USB audio interface: up to 32 outputs via a supported class-compliant interface. Lightning devices need an Apple Lightning Digital AV Adapter; USB-C devices need an Apple USB-C Digital AV Multiport Adapter. Add a powered USB hub if the interface is bus-powered. Outputs are grouped into custom buses, mono or stereo.

Option 3 - networked audio (Dante, SoundGrid): connect the Playback device to a network running that protocol. iPad and iPhone support only two channels over networked audio; macOS apps like Dante Virtual Soundcard can route up to 32 channels.
Use an in-ear monitoring solution so click and guide are not heard by the congregation. Accompaniment tracks do not include click and guide.

results.title: How To | Track & Bus Routing in Playback
results.summary: Playback has dedicated Click and Guide buses by default. Bus routing and MultiOuts require a Playback Premium subscription. Playback groups 150+ instruments into 16 buses plus a dedicated SMPTE bus; each bus can go to any available output on the selected audio device, mono or stereo. The Pad bus cannot be re-routed. Track routing is saved per device and applies globally to that track; it is not saved with setlists or named arrangements. Separate buses assigned to the same output still share that hardware feed. For independent external control, use distinct available outputs matching the caller's connected desk channels; example output numbers are not universal assignments.

steps.text: Route tracks to buses: Settings > Tracks tab, assign each track to a bus (defaults are preset and can be overwritten).
Route buses to outputs: Settings > Buses tab, tap a bus row and choose an available output.
Route several buses at once: tap 'Assign Multiple Busses' in the bottom-right, select buses, assign one output.
Rename a bus: drag its row to the left to reveal Edit.
Greyed-out output: the SMPTE bus is probably using it. Disable SMPTE in the General tab or set the SMPTE bus to 'None'.

Alternative from the main interface: open the 'Busses' layer (bottom right next to the master fader, or cycle layers with the button beside it), tap Edit (top right) to enter Setlist/Song Map edit mode, tap a bus name and select the output.
Bus mixes are song-specific by default; disable Song Specific Buses in Settings for a global mix. Solo/mute on a bus affects all tracks routed to it.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > App Overview > Login Requirements > Organizations vs. Users
results.text: An organization in the MultiTracks.com ecosystem is the umbrella under which content can be purchased, users can be added, and subscriptions can be shared. When an 'account' is created using the "Sign Up" flow, an organization and a user is created simultaneously and the user is set as the owner of the organization. When logging into Playback, there is an organization selection prompt, to select which organization to log into. If you are a user belonging only to the organization created when you built your account, then select that organization. However, a user can be added to other existing MultiTracks.com organizations and have access to content belonging to those organizations in Playback. Every organization that you've been added to will be available at this login screen.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Building a Setlist > The Setlists Menu > Navigating the Setlists menu
results.text:
Tap the Setlists Icon in the top-right of the transport section of Playback, to open the Setlists menu. The currently opened setlist can be renamed, saved to the cloud and accessed from anywhere else in the ecosystem, and more from this menu.

The setlist menu is where new setlists can be created, imported from Planning Center, or existing setlists can be opened. It's where all setlist management takes place in the Playback app. The Setlists menu also has options to "Delete All Setlists From Device" to clear out all local setlist data for a particular Playback app. (Deleting all setlists from a device in Playback does not delete the setlists from the organization).

To Open a previously saved setlist, tap Open Setlist and search for the setlist by name or select from upcoming or past setlists by date.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > App Overview > Login Requirements > Organizational Content Permissions
results.text:
If you are logging into your own organization, then you are ready to start downloading your organization’s purchased content or Rental credits immediately. When logging into another organization, certain permission subscriptions need to be added to your account in order for you to access purchased tracks, spend Rental credits, or save Cloud changes to setlists, song arrangements, and MIDI Cues.

For more information about managing your organization’s team members, subscriptions, and content permissions, check out: 📖 Managing Roles and Permissions

Once logged in, you’re ready to start building a setlist!
